declaration: void __thiscall EditorCreatureController_SetTargetPosition_0059b0f0(EditorCreatureController *this, Vector3 *position, bool applyNow, bool ignoreZ);

mechanics: Copy position->x/y/z into controller+0x20, controller+0x24 and controller+0x28, then repeat the same three words into controller+0x2c, controller+0x30 and controller+0x34.

Magnitude guard on the 0x2c triple: FSQRT of the summed squares, then FLD of the constant at 0x013f64b0 (5.0f), then FXCH so ST0 is the length and ST1 is 5.0. FCOMIP ST0,ST1 sets CF when length < 5.0, and JBE additionally covers equality, so the JBE at 0x0059b1b3 skips the rescale whenever length <= 5.0. The rescale therefore runs only when 5.0f < length: long vectors are scaled DOWN to length 5 and short vectors are left untouched. An earlier revision had the comparison inverted and stretched short vectors instead.
Rescale form is (component * (1/length)) * 5.0f, matching the three chained MULSS rather than a single fused multiply.
When ignoreZ is non-zero, store 0.0f into controller+0x34; this happens after the magnitude guard.
When applyNow is zero, return immediately: no creature write, no raycast, no notification.
Otherwise copy the 0x2c triple into creature+0x04, creature+0x08 and creature+0x0c, then copy the same triple into controller+0x38, controller+0x3c and controller+0x40.
When ignoreZ is non-zero the downward raycast is skipped entirely.

Otherwise build the query: 0x0067dd80 returns the picker world, its vtable slot 0x28 is called with (0x026f3933, false), and the returned index seeds a bit in a zeroed 64-bit mask only when it is below 0x40. The query flag byte is 4.
The ray origin is (creature+0x04, creature+0x08, 0x01465544 - 0x013ec5b4) = (x, y, 500.0f - 1000.0f) = z of -500.0f, giving a fixed top-down drop.
Call shadow->vtable[0x24] with eight arguments; a non-zero result writes hit.x into creature+0x0c, so the ground contact only ever touches the z component.
Finally call 0x00a047d0 on the creature with the constant 1.
Epilogue is POP ESI/EBX, ADD ESP,0x3c, RET 0xc; the frame is a fixed 0x3c because the raycast arguments are all stack-resident.

evidence.observation: FSQRT; FLD [0x013f64b0]; FXCH; FCOMIP ST0,ST1; FSTP ST0; JBE 0x0059b1b3 settles the guard: FXCH puts the length in ST0 and 5.0 in ST1, and JBE is taken when length <= 5.0.
Listing also fixes the two triple copies, the [ESP+0x50] ignoreZ and [ESP+0x4c] applyNow loads, the eight-argument raycast and the RET 0xc epilogue.
Constants are 5.0f, 500.0f and 1000.0f, confirming the -500.0f ray origin.
Nine direct call sites; the only in-module caller is 0x0059cf00.

evidence: FCOMIP ST0,ST1 at 0x0059b13e compares the x87 magnitude against 5.0 and JBE at 0x0059b142 skips the rescale. FCOMIP sets CF/ZF/PF on an unordered compare, so a NaN magnitude takes the JBE branch and the value is left unchanged. The guard is therefore an ORDERED 5.0 < length test; C++ >= is unordered-false for NaN and would rescale it, so the body uses !(5.0f < length).

The slot +0x24 call site pushes eight stack words (0x0059b2bc and 0x0059bf76): 0, 0, pointer, 0, pointer, 0, pointer, out, giving the declared order (out, origin, word, query, word, aux, word, word). Both call sites pass all eight and both output records are read.

The ray-query record base is the ESP-relative slot 0x6c. Five zeroed words are stored at record +0x00, +0x04, +0x08, +0x0c and +0x10 (0x0059bed6-0x0059bee6) and the collision bit is OR'd through LEA EDX,[ESP+ECX*0x4+0x6c] at 0x0059bf18, so the collision words start at record offset 0x00, not 0x10. Read in forward address order the two flag stores are 0x0059bef2 writing byte 4 to [ESP+0x80] (record +0x14) and 0x0059beea writing byte 0 to [ESP+0x81] (record +0x15), giving flag_14=4 and flag_15=0. OpaqueRayQuery is therefore five collision words at 0x00 with flag_14 and flag_15, giving a 0x18-byte record. 0x0059b0f0 uses base 0x2c and stores byte 4 to +0x14 (0x0059b240) and 0 to +0x15 (0x0059b23c), so both bodies share one flag pair.
tests: long offset (length 13) is scaled down to length 5 componentwise with the (x*(1/len))*5 form
the exact 5.0 boundary is not rescaled
ignoreZ zeroes 0x34 after the magnitude guard and leaves the raw 0x20 copy unclamped
applyNow false performs no creature write, no raycast and no notification
applyNow true writes the creature position and the 0x38 triple in that order
ignoreZ true skips the raycast entirely and still notifies
ray origin is (creature.x, creature.y, -500.0f) and the query flag byte is 4
a collision index below 0x40 seeds the matching mask bit; an index of 0x40 or above seeds nothing
a non-zero raycast result writes the hit x into creature+0x0c and the notification argument is 1
offset rescale uses an ordered comparison so a NaN magnitude is returned unchanged
raycast slot +0x24 receives all eight native stack words and both out records are read
ray-query record is five collision words at offset 0x00 with the flag byte at 0x14 (value 4)
